extracted.intended_audience: Citizens and readers assessing the proposed U.S. Constitution (original American public, especially New Yorkers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts principles and standards used to judge constitutional arrangements for impeachment trials, Senate powers, appointments, and the mode of electing the President. Focuses on practical safeguards, institutional balance, and textual/structural interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentrating impeachment adjudicative power in few judges
rubrics_metrics.description: The awful discretion which a court of impeachments must necessarily have ... forbids the commitment of the trust to a small number of persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impeachment decisions can doom honor or infamy of the most distinguished characters; a small, permanent judicial body would lack sufficient checks and risk misuse of discretion. Preference for numerous, representative judges to limit arbitrary power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve double security by separating accusatory and adjudicatory roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The division of them between the two branches of the legislature, assigning to one the right of accusing, to the other the right of judging, avoids the inconvenience of making the same persons both accusers and judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having the House institute impeachments and the Senate try them prevents persecution from a factious spirit and avoids bias of combined accuser-judge. This separation is presented as essential to protect innocence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make the same persons judges in both impeachment and ordinary prosecutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Would it be proper that the persons who had disposed of his fame ... should, in another trial, for the same offense, be also the disposers of his life and his fortune?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the same body pronounces on impeachment and then sits indirectly to affect later criminal proceedings, prior bias could influence subsequent trials or juries; this risks denying the double security intended by separate trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Senate as court of impeachments over Supreme Court
rubrics_metrics.description: These considerations seem alone sufficient to authorize a conclusion, that the Supreme Court would have been an improper substitute for the Senate, as a court of impeachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments: Supreme Court would be too small, no jury between judges and punished party, and judges might exercise awful discretion without sufficient counterbalance. The Senate, being more numerous and political, is a more appropriate tribunal for this special purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make chief justice preside rather than incorporate the whole Supreme Court
rubrics_metrics.description: To a certain extent, the benefits of that union will be obtained from making the chief justice of the Supreme Court the president of the court of impeachments ... while the inconveniences of an entire incorporation ... will be substantially avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single presiding judicial officer (chief justice) secures some judicial voice without importing the full judiciary into the impeachment function, avoiding the drawbacks of full judicial incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject creation of a separate permanent impeachment court as impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: A court formed upon such a plan, would either be attended with a heavy expense, or might in practice be subject to a variety of casualties and inconveniences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent officers would require fixed stipends and be expensive; ad hoc state officers would be hard to assemble, cause delays, and create opportunities for intrigue and corruption. These practical difficulties counsel against a distinct standing court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept pragmatic, non‑perfect constitutional design over unattainable perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: If mankind were to resolve to agree in no institution of government, until every part of it had been adjusted to the most exact standard of perfection, society would soon become a general scene of anarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques that show some clauses are not the best imaginable do not suffice to reject the plan; the standard is whether the plan is good on the whole and practicable, not whether every provision is ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑thirds concurrence for conviction as security for innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: As the concurrence of two thirds of the Senate will be requisite to a condemnation, the security to innocence, from this additional circumstance, will be as complete as itself can desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High supermajority requirement is cited as an important structural safeguard against wrongful conviction in political trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial intermixture of departments is compatible with separation of powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The true meaning of this maxim ... has been shown to be entirely compatible with a partial intermixture of those departments for special purposes, preserving them, in the main, distinct and unconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation of powers allows limited overlap (e.g., Senate trying impeachments) when that overlap serves mutual defense of branches; absolute separation is neither feasible nor desirable for all functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate each power on its own merits rather than vague aggregate fears
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be more safe, as well as more simple, to dismiss such vague and uncertain calculations, to examine each power by itself, and to decide, on general principles, where it may be deposited with most advantage and least inconvenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections that the Senate will become 'too aristocratic' are dismissed as imprecise; instead assess the practical effects and counterbalances of each specific power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterbalance Senate powers by House prerogatives and other structural checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusive privilege of originating money bills will belong to the House ... The same house will possess the sole right of instituting impeachments ... The same house will be the umpire in all elections of the President ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distribution of powers (money bills, impeachment initiation, contingent presidential election) is presented as intentional counterweights that prevent Senate predominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate's confirmation role is ratify/reject, not active selection
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be the office of the President to NOMINATE, and, with the advice and consent of the Senate, to APPOINT ... They may defeat one choice of the Executive, and oblige him to make another; but they cannot themselves CHOOSE, they can only ratify or reject the choice of the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural limitation reduces the danger of favoritism: senators generally lack incentive to protect nominees beyond evidences of merit, because they cannot directly place their own favorites by appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recess appointment clause applies to 'officers' not to senators; state executives fill Senate vacancies
rubrics_metrics.description: The clause ... cannot be understood to comprehend the power of filling vacancies in the Senate ... the Senate of the United States shall be composed ... chosen BY THE LEGISLATURE THEREOF ... if vacancies ... DURING THE RECESS OF THE LEGISLATURE OF ANY STATE, the Executive THEREOF may make temporary appointments ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual/structural interpretation: the temporary presidential appointment power is supplemental to appointment of officers whose appointments are otherwise provided for, and the Constitution explicitly assigns temporary senatorial vacancies to state executives, refuting claims of presidential power to fill Senate seats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Members of collective deliberative bodies should be exempt from punishment for acts done in a collective capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is essential to the freedom and to the necessary independence of the deliberations of the body, that the members of it should be exempt from punishment for acts done in a collective capacity;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective immunity for legislative acts is justified to preserve independence of deliberation; societal security depends on confiding important trusts to proper hands and making combination against public good difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral College design: balance popular input, deliberation, stability, and protection from corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: It was desirable that the sense of the people should operate ... by committing the right of making it, not to any preestablished body, but to men chosen by the people ... that the immediate election should be made by men most capable of analyzing the qualities ... to afford as little opportunity as possible to tumult and disorder ... oppose to cabal, intrigue, and corruption ... excluded from eligibility ... all those who from situation might be suspected of too great devotion to the President in office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages listed: (1) reflects popular will via electors chosen for purpose; (2) small, deliberative electors better analyze qualifications; (3) electors assemble in state to reduce contagion of passions; (4) dispersed electors resist sudden corruption and foreign influence; (5) eligibility restrictions (no current senators/representatives/officers) reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral mechanism includes contingency procedure to ensure a majority outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Their votes ... the person who may happen to have a majority of the whole number of votes will be the President. But ... it is provided that, in such a contingency, the House of Representatives shall select out of the candidates who shall have the five highest number of votes, the man who in their opinion may be best qualified for the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingent selection by House among top five vote-getters prevents indecisive plurality outcomes; design ensures a definite selection and encourages broadly acceptable candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design the Executive to be independent of other branches for tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: Another and no less important desideratum was, that the Executive should be independent for his continuance in office on all but the people themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence from legislative or other branches in tenure reduces temptation to sacrifice duty for popularity with those controlling reappointment; electoral structure should protect executive independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vice‑President election method preserves state representation and casting vote utility
rubrics_metrics.description: One is, that to secure at all times the possibility of a definite resolution of the body, it is necessary that the President should have only a casting vote. ... as the Vice-President may occasionally become a substitute for the President, ... all the reasons which recommend the mode of election prescribed for the one, apply ... to the manner of appointing the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting the Vice‑President by the same broader electoral method (rather than from Senate) prevents loss of a state's constant vote and ensures the VP is chosen with considerations similar to those for the President (deliberation, independence, competence).
